title: Editorial: health in a changing climate
content:
Abstract
Climate change is an escalating public health crisis. This special collection assembles 7 research articles on health and climate change, looking at risks, solutions, and opportunities, sparking dialogue and inspiring action for a healthier, more equitable future in a changing climate.The collection explores climate-health risks and responses across diverse contexts. A literature review examining the intersection of climate change, food insecurity and conflict shows that global health policy fails to address these overlapping crises together. A systematic review of cooling centres to prevent heat-related illness and mortality identifies evidence gaps, underscoring the need for rigorous, real-world evaluation. Research on the 2015–2018 Western Cape drought in South Africa demonstrates how leadership and effective governance, infrastructure and cross-sectoral collaboration strengthen health system resilience in the face of climate disasters. Research from Southern Brazil explores seasonal patterns in schizophrenia hospitalisations, suggesting the risks climate change may pose to the mind.The collection also covers healthcare decarbonisation. A mixed-methods study in Kenya finds health workers eager for climate action but limited by training and institutional support. A co-created theory of change from Catalonia, Spain, highlights participatory governance and local adaptation for carbon-neutral healthcare. A perspective on noise pollution identifies opportunities to integrate noise reduction into climate policies.By integrating health into climate policy and treating every climate shift as a health priority, humanity can move beyond mere survival. This collection serves as both a warning and a blueprint, showing that while the challenges are systemic, the solutions are within our reach when high-level ambition and local action move in tandem.
